purpose: Persist the sources used to verify the Skiptvet church coordinate, medieval building identity, fire history, later building layers and current-use constraints.

legacyCoordinate.assessment: Undocumented point approximately 988.3 metres north-north-west of the church.

identityResolution.entityType: standing Romanesque medieval stone church rebuilt after the 1762 fire

supports: Romanesque nave, chancel and west-tower base
Romanesque stone church from the twelfth century

chronology.event: The Romanesque stone church was built and dedicated to the Virgin Mary.
A fire destroyed the timber and interior; the south wall was heavily damaged and the church was rebuilt.
The present wooden porch and sacristy were built.
Much of the interior furnishing was renewed.
Harald Sund and Ulrik Hendriksen completed a major restoration.

interpretationLimits: Year 1200 is approximate; sources place the church in the twelfth century or around 1200.
The 1762 fire caused extensive rebuilding but did not erase the entire medieval stone structure.
The canonical point represents the church building, not the entire churchyard or Kirkebakken.
The rectory and the 1936 grave chapel are separate components.
Services, confirmations, funerals and cemetery use take priority over gameplay.
